summary: Atomic validation checkers that implement the Checker behaviour for publishing-industry data integrity: ONIX codelist membership, ISBN-13 and GTIN-14 check-digit algorithms, ISO-639 language codes, ISO-4217 currency codes, and non-empty presence. These plug into the validation rule DSL used primarily by the OnixEdit plugin.

intentions.title: Enforce publishing-industry data standards at ingest
intentions.evidence: isbn13_checksum.ex and gtin14_checksum.ex implement the exact GS1/ISBN check-digit algorithms; codelist_ref.ex validates values against versioned ONIX codelists (e.g. ContributorRole list 17 issue 73) — all guard the integrity of book metadata destined for Bokbasen/ONIX export

intentions.title: Keep boot-path validation zero-dependency
intentions.evidence: iso639_language.ex and iso4217_currency.ex use compile-time MapSets with hardcoded publishing-relevant subsets explicitly because the full codelist registry (WI3) is not available at boot; modules comment this design choice directly

intentions.title: Make validation composable via a uniform Checker behaviour
intentions.evidence: Every module declares @behaviour Barkpark.Validation.Checker and implements a single check/2 returning :ok | {:error, atom}, making them interchangeable atoms in the rule DSL rather than ad-hoc guard clauses

intentions.title: Surface version-aware codelist mismatches rather than silent failures
intentions.evidence: codelist_ref.ex distinguishes :codelist_version_mismatch (list exists but wrong issue) from :codelist_unknown_value (value absent), letting rule authors give actionable errors when ONIX codelist versions drift
